summary: SpaceX aims to launch its next Starship test flight this month and attempt a booster catch as the company prepares to begin orbital operations, while NASA and SpaceX study methods to prevent future upper-stage lunar collisions following a scheduled moon impact. In international defense developments, Telesat secured a $1.63 billion contract to provide Arctic satellite communications for Canada, while Rocket Lab and STR won U.S. Space Force contracts for airborne-target tracking. Strategic military infrastructure also expanded as the Department of the Air Force allied with the Texas Space Commission, K2 was selected to host Space Force satellite laser link testing, and private investors acquired a majority stake in L3Harris’ propulsion business, re-establishing Rocketdyne as a standalone entity. In civil government and commercial space, preliminary data from NASA’s PUNCH mission demonstrated improved solar storm forecasting capabilities, NOAA contracted to purchase Spire hyperspectral microwave sounder data, and startup Xona cleared its final regulatory hurdle for a satellite positioning constellation. Readers should watch next for SpaceX’s scheduled early Aug. 5 launch carrying three BlueBird direct-to-cell satellites.
